title: Reasoning-Based Refinement of Unsupervised Text Clusters with LLMs
subcategory: LLM as semantic judge for post-hoc cluster refinement and labelling
task: Refinement and labelling of unsupervised text clusters (social media discourse)
problem: Unsupervised clustering outputs contain incoherent, redundant or poorly grounded clusters that are hard to validate without labels.
architecture: TF-IDF + HDBSCAN cluster proposals refined by GPT-4o in three reasoning stages: coherence verification of cluster summaries, pairwise redundancy adjudication (merge/reject), and two-stage label grounding (generate then consolidate labels).
llm_or_encoder: GPT-4o (also Llama 3.2 and Mistral Large 2 for assignment); SBERT for the baseline refinement

datasets.name: X (Twitter)
datasets.details: vegan discourse; 20000 tweets from 275 users sampled from 330464 tweets

key_results: Silhouette rises from 0.122 (HDBSCAN) to 0.674 on X and from -0.017 to 0.979 on Bluesky after LLM refinement.
Human-judged assignment accuracy with GPT-4o: 78.4% (X) and 89.8% (Bluesky) vs 72.8 / 68.4 for TopicGPT and 38.7 / 42.4 for BERTopic; inter-annotator agreement 0.82.
strengths: Human evaluation and statistical testing in a label-free setting.

limitations.text: English social-media data from one discourse domain (veganism).
LLM judgements may carry human biases; no fine-tuning of LLMs.
Initial clusters use TF-IDF; dense encoders not tested as proposal generators.
SBERT refinement achieves better separation (DBi) on X than LLM refinement.

notes: Cross-platform robustness analysis under matched temporal/volume conditions.
